description: We are a team of enthusiastic Computer Science students passionate about space technology, innovation, and problem-solving. We enjoy web development, exploring new technologies, and building creative solutions using NASA data. We welcome passionate beginners and are looking for teammates skilled in React, Python, AI/ML, UI/UX design, data analysis, research, and presentation. Let's learn, innovate, and explore the universe together!
summary: Mars Survival Navigator is an interactive educational prototype for planning astronaut traverses in Jezero Crater using real NASA orbital data. It loads a verified 5.04 × 5.04 km crop of MRO CTX terrain (20 m DTM + 6 m orthomosaic centered on the Jezero delta and Perseverance landing area) into a 252×252 metric grid, then compares two A* route strategies — shortest distance vs. terrain-aware slope cost — with elevation profiles, a traverse playback inspector, and multi-waypoint science stops. A lazy-loaded CesiumJS Mars globe (R = 3,396.19 km ellipsoid) drapes the same data as a 3D relief mesh at true scale, with camera presets and vertical exaggeration. Sourced context cards cover MOLA, THEMIS, and SWIM — explicitly labeled historical/regional, never live telemetry. Every output carries provenance and a clear disclaimer: terrain-aware ≠ safe, orbital data ≠ surface survey.
details: What it does: Pick start/end cells (or science destinations) on real Jezero terrain, optionally add up to 3 ordered waypoints, and compute both shortest-distance and terrain-aware routes via a Web Worker running 8-neighbor A*. Results include distance, ascent/descent, mean/max slope, steep-slope exposure fraction, cumulative elevation profiles, and step-by-step cell inspection. A hazard overlay highlights cells above a declared slope threshold, and a trade-off badge quantifies distance cost vs. exposure reduction. 3D overview: A lazy-loaded CesiumJS globe renders Mars as a sphere (R = 3,396.19 m — never WGS84), with the CTX crop as a textured relief mesh built from the actual elevation grid, science pins, and route polylines elevated to terrain height. 1×/3× exaggeration toggle, graticule, and camera presets. Falls back to the 2D planner on any WebGL failure. Scientific honesty: The app separates verified data (dataKind: "real") from a labelled synthetic fixture, which is pruned from production builds and rejected by a boundary gate. Slope is a planning preference, not a safety rating; no weather, oxygen, or radiation telemetry is shown. THEMIS/SWIM are historical regional context only. Tools: React + TypeScript + Vite, Leaflet (CRS.Simple local grid), CesiumJS 1.147 (offline assets), Recharts, Vitest, Python/rasterio for data preparation. ~40 unit tests + Playwright E2E smoke tests.
